entries.claim: A held edit to a field that re-enumerates (mode, filter, oversampling) is stored without being applied or re-mirrored. Later held edits for list-dependent fields therefore carry enumeration IDs from the pre-switch lists. On flush those IDs are sent after the mode or filter switch has replaced the lists, so they name a different entry or none.
entries.failure_scenario: The app is not ready (ready false; the dim is opacity only, per tokens.css .app.offline, so the controls stay usable). The user sets mode to a new value; writeLive holds it and returns, with no remirrorLive and no liveBusy, so liveEnumBusy never disables the filter control and enums keeps the old mode's lists. The user then picks a filter, so View.js:175 holds an ID from the old list. Easy Mode is worse: easylane.js:147 resolves the filter name against liveControls() on the assumption that the preceding writeLive re-mirrored. The name is either missing from the old list (silently dropped) or resolves to an old-list ID. Once ready, flushHeld sends mode first (Map insertion order), the engine re-enumerates, and then sends the filter with the stale ID. remirrorLive's own comment says this posts 'an ID from a list the engine had already replaced', so the engine selects a filter the user never chose. If the user edits filter first and mode second, the Map keeps filter first, so the newest filter goes out before mode and the mode switch then overwrites it.

entries.claim: flushHeld commits to its snapshot batch and sends every entry without checking sendable() again and without checking whether the user has since written that field directly. A held value can therefore go out against a lane that is no longer ready, or after a newer edit and overwrite it.
entries.failure_scenario: (a) Held: filter=25, shaper=31. ready turns true and the flush awaits sendLive('filter'). While that round trip runs, sendable is true, so the user's new shaper=50 goes straight out through sendLive. The flush then sends shaper=31, and the engine ends on the stale value the user had already replaced. (b) Held: mode, filter, shaper. SetMode takes the engine down briefly (state.js comment), the next health poll reads ready false or an apply sets engineRestarting, and the loop still posts the remaining held writes. The server's readiness gate refuses them; each edit is reported as an error and dropped, not held again for the next ready.
